avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the Old Town; usual nightlife scam caution

hood_desc: The exquisitely preserved medieval walled town of cobbled lanes, guild halls, spires and Town Hall Square; suits first-time visitors wanting fairy-tale atmosphere and walkable sights.
A hip, bohemian former-industrial district by the sea with wooden houses, the Telliskivi creative city, cafes and street food; suits younger travelers, creatives and foodies.
An elegant, green district around the baroque Kadriorg Palace and park with art museums and stately villas; suits culture lovers and those wanting a calm, refined base.
A seaside residential district northeast of the center with a beach, marina and the Pirita convent ruins; suits families and warmer-season visitors wanting sand and quiet.
A revamped former-industrial quarter between Old Town and the port, with striking modern architecture, design shops and restaurants; suits design-minded travelers wanting central contemporary buzz.
lodging: Oru Hub Hotel Tallinn - Handwritten Collection

water.note: Tap water is safe and considered some of the best quality in the Baltics.

transit.pay: Visitors can tap a contactless bank card on the validator when boarding (fare is calculated automatically), or buy a paper ticket from the driver (~€2) or top up an ühiskaart card via the Pilet.ee app/kiosks. Public transit is free for registered Tallinn residents, but tourists and non-residents must always pay.
transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 5:30am-midnight, with a handful of night bus routes on weekends.
transit.note: Tallinn public transit is free for registered residents, but visitors must buy a ticket or tap a bank card every ride.

landmarks: Tallinn Town Hall Square (Raekoja plats)
The medieval heart of Old Town, ringed by colorful merchant houses and cafés, especially charming during Christmas markets.
Toompea Castle
A hilltop medieval fortress that now houses Estonia's parliament, with pink Baroque façade and pink towers.
Alexander Nevsky Cathedral
An ornate Russian Orthodox cathedral with onion domes, striking against Toompea's skyline.
St. Olaf's Church (Oleviste)
Once among the world's tallest buildings, its soaring spire remains a defining feature of Tallinn's skyline.
Kohtuotsa Viewing Platform
A popular Toompea overlook offering the classic panoramic photo of Old Town's red-tiled roofs and spires.
Kadriorg Palace
An 18th-century Baroque palace built by Peter the Great, set within elegant landscaped gardens.
Tallinn Town Hall (Raekoda)
One of the best-preserved Gothic town halls in Northern Europe, topped by the iconic 'Old Thomas' weathervane.
Viru Gate
Twin medieval stone towers marking a historic entrance to Old Town, a classic photo spot along the city walls.
Kiek in de Kök Tower
A formidable medieval artillery tower offering city wall walks and views over the fortifications.
St. Mary's Cathedral (Toomkirik)
Estonia's oldest church, a Gothic landmark on Toompea Hill with a distinctive Baroque spire.

train.note: No international trains run from Tallinn: the St Petersburg and Moscow services are suspended due to sanctions, and the Rail Baltica line to Riga and Warsaw is not due to open until around 2030. Elron runs domestic trains from Balti jaam (Baltic Station) to Tartu, Narva and Parnu. For the other Baltic capitals, take a coach.

bus.note: Frequent international coaches leave from Tallinn Bus Station (Autobussijaam). Lux Express and Ecolines link Tallinn with Riga, Vilnius and Warsaw, plus St Petersburg for travellers holding the right Russian visa.

ferry.note: Ferries sail from the Port of Tallinn (Old City Harbour). Helsinki is just 2-2.5h and runs many times a day year-round; the Stockholm boat is an overnight cruise-ferry via the Aland Islands.
